unit_label: BRBL C U03: Distinguish the section 13 notice stage from the possession-measure remedy

facts.locator: printed pp.244-245 / PDF pp.263-264; primary decision separately cited
facts.statement: Hindon Forge paragraphs9-11 distinguish section13(2)/(3A) from measures; paragraph17 and conclusion at PDF69 permit section17 at rule8(1)/(2) possession notice rather than awaiting physical dispossession.

facts.locator: paragraph8, PDF pp.36-43; paragraphs9-11 pp.43-45; paragraph17 pp.51-52; deciding conclusion PDF p.69
facts.statement: The Supreme Court distinguishes the earlier deposit ruling and demand stage; concluding decision recognises section17 remedy at rule8(1)/(2) possession-notice stage. Quoted contrary High Court position is rejected, not adopted.

payload.title: A statutory safeguard depends on the event that has happened
payload.core_explanation_md:
A demand notice, consideration of objections and a possession measure are different events. In Hindon Forge the Supreme Court distinguishes the section 13(2) demand/section 13(3A) response stage from measures under section 13(4). Its conclusion recognises approach to the DRT under section 17 at the possession-notice stage described in rule 8(1) and 8(2).

Do not turn this into a requirement to wait for actual physical dispossession or completed sale before seeking that statutory remedy. Nor should it be read as saying every earlier letter is already a section 13(4) measure. This card describes the identified decision; later authority and the facts of a live proceeding require review.

self_check.prompt_text: Must a borrower always wait until physical eviction to use the remedy described in Hindon Forge?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The specified possession-notice stage can suffice.

payload.stem_md: Under the stated Hindon Forge holding, a borrower receives the rule 8(1)/(2) possession notice. A file note says section 17 is unavailable solely because physical possession has not yet changed. What needs correction?

options.text_md: The borrower must wait for the auction buyer to take possession
options.explanation_md: The holding rejects physical-dispossession waiting as a necessary bar at this stage.

options.text_md: A bank internal email is always enough to prove a possession measure
options.explanation_md: The relevant statutory notice/measure must actually be established.

options.text_md: The stated possession-notice stage can support the section 17 approach
options.explanation_md: The Supreme Court expressly recognises the remedy at this stage.

options.text_md: The judgment removes every procedural requirement of section 17
options.explanation_md: It addresses the disputed timing point, not abandonment of all requirements.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The Supreme Court expressly recognises the remedy at this stage.

payload.stem_md: A file contains only a demand notice and rejection of a representation, with no stipulated section 13(4) measure. Why is it unsafe to label it identical to the possession-notice case?

options.text_md: The demand/response stage and the possession measure are distinct procedural events
options.explanation_md: The cited judgment distinguishes them; the actual event must be identified.

options.text_md: A demand notice always transfers legal ownership to the bank
options.explanation_md: Notice alone is not a completed ownership transfer.

options.text_md: A rejected representation automatically proves a completed auction
options.explanation_md: Those are different steps with different evidence.

options.text_md: Every correspondence date is the date of physical dispossession
options.explanation_md: The nature of the act cannot be inferred from a date alone.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The cited judgment distinguishes them; the actual event must be identified.
